The listed-building-grade dataset states that all data is authoritative.
The article-4 specification requires both direction and direction-area datasets.
Article-4 data may be supplied as CSV, GeoJSON, GML or GeoPackage.
Article-4 data may also be served through OGC WFS or ArcGIS API.
Each direction reference must be unique and permanent.
A direction record includes a URL for the authoritative order or notice.
Each direction area requires polygon or multipolygon geometry.
Article-4-area geometry must use WGS84 coordinates.
The tree-preservation specification defines order, zone and individual-tree datasets.
The tree-preservation-order dataset is supplied as CSV.
Zone and tree data may be supplied as CSV, GeoJSON, GML or GeoPackage.
Each tree-preservation zone requires a unique permanent reference.
Each zone record links to its covering tree-preservation order.
The 1 metre composite DTM covers approximately 99% of England.
The composite DTM has 1 metre spatial resolution.
The DTM is based on the last or only laser return.
Surface objects are removed from the DSM to create the terrain model.
Terrain extraction also uses manual editing.
The current composite was produced by the Environment Agency in 2022.
The composite combines Time Stamped archive and National LiDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat surveys exist, the newest suitable best-resolution data is used.
Resampled data is processed using bilinear interpolation.
The composite survey period runs from 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022.
Metadata index catalogues identify the source survey used at a location.
The DTM is available as GeoTIFF raster data.
Downloads are organised into 5 kilometre tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
Elevation values are presented in metres.
Heights are referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
The composite uses the OSTN15 transformation method.
Input surveys have stated vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE.
The metadata reports no public-access constraint beyond the licence.
The metadata lists annual update frequency.
The published coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
The dataset exposes a WMS resource.

The dataset exposes a WCS resource.

The 1 metre composite DSM includes terrain and surface objects.
DSM surface objects include vehicles, buildings and vegetation.
The DSM uses last-return or only-return pulses.
The 1 metre DSM covers approximately 99% of England.
The DSM metadata states vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE.
OS Terrain 5 is a detailed digital terrain model of Great Britain.
The product is supplied as both gridded heights and contours.
Scheduled publication months are January, April, July and October.
Grid and contour data are supplied in 5 kilometre by 5 kilometre tiles.
The grid has regular 5 metre post spacing.
Standard contours use 5 metre vertical intervals.
Grid data is available as ASCII grid and GML 3.2.1.
Contours and spot heights are available as Esri shapefile or GML 3.2.1.
The national grid supply contains 10,579 data tiles.
The national contour supply contains 10,572 data tiles.
National supplies are ZIP-compressed and not encrypted.
A full compressed national grid supply is approximately 16 GB.
The source terrain model is captured as a triangulated irregular network.
The source TIN uses mass points and breaklines.
The source DTM removes buildings, supported structures and vegetation from bare earth.
Contour GML stores heights in the INSPIRE-derived propertyValue attribute.
